It loads aggregates through injected domain repository interfaces. It hands the business decisions to domain objects: RegistrationPolicy.assertCanRegister, workshop.takeSeat/releaseSeat and registration.cancel. It saves the results and maps them to application DTOs. The NestJS @Injectable/@Inject decorators are allowed here, because the rubric only bans framework decorators in domain files. The constructor parameters are dependency wiring. No method signature uses a request, response, HTTP context, status code or HTTP error from a web package or the delivery layer. The only error thrown is the project's own DomainError. The optional `context?: WorkshopOfContextDto` parameter is an interface the project declares in this same file, holding only `requestId?: string`. It is not a framework or transport type, and the rubric says a project-declared type is not a framework type whatever its name. The clone flags point to duplicated code between workshopOf and WorkshopsService.findOne. That is a duplication concern, not a layer-role problem, so it does not count against this rule.
